chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yaqteen from al-Husayn ibn Khalid, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, the people say: The guarantor is the debtor.' He said, 'He said, "There is no penalty on the guarantor; the penalty is on the one who consumes the wealth."'
ai.seo_question: Who bears the financial liability in a guarantee contract according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) refutes the colloquial maxim 'the guarantor is the debtor' by establishing that financial liability (*ghurm*) attaches to the beneficiary of the wealth rather than the mere guarantor. This distinction is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for differentiating between the contract of guarantee (*kafala*) and the underlying debt, ensuring that the guarantor is not unfairly burdened if the primary debtor defaults, provided they did not consume the asset themselves.
